messages:
emily_support: FYI customer AcmePay (tenant T-ACME-41) reporting widespread 504s and timeouts starting ~09:10 PT. They see errors hitting the hosted gateway (us-west-2) and are blocking production flows. Ticket CS-8421.
emily_support: They say ~100-130 rps but the majority are very long-context requests (~8k+ tokens) and some streaming. Attaching the quick gateway excerpt below.
emily_support: ```
[gateway] 2025-06-23T16:09:58Z tenant=T-ACME-41 req=abc123 status=504 backend_err=dequeue_timeout queue_depth=120 max_queue=128
[batcher] 2025-06-23T16:10:01Z batch_id=789 wait_ms=3200 hold_on_long_seq=true kvcache_evictions=27
[runtime] 2025-06-23T16:10:02Z worker=gw-12 processing_seq_len=8124 tok_gen_ms=2100
```
emily_support: Customer is seeing ~30% request failures and they want ETA. Can infra/runtime advise quick mitigation?

raj_infra: Looking now. Initial glance: queue_depth near hard limit (128). Continuous-batching metrics show a backlog: batchers are waiting on long-seq requests, which inflates batch wait and holds workers. Head-of-line blocking.
raj_infra: Probable cause: long sequence requests monopolizing KV cache and GPU workers -> queue fills -> gateway returns early 504s/timeouts.

maria_runtime: +1. We saw similar pattern last quarter. Long sequences + streaming = batchers keep open until completion. That increases p99 and eats concurrency.
maria_runtime: Do we have tenant-specific concurrency/seq-length caps for hosted? If not, we should apply an emergency throttle.

lee_oncall: oncall-bot shows multiple backpressure alerts: :warning:
oncall-bot: "ingress.queue.depth[T-ACME-41] > 0.9 * max_queue for 4m"

kevin_sre: Suggested quick mitigations (short-term):
- Apply tenant throttle: set max_concurrency=2 and reduce max_seq_len to 4096 for T-ACME-41
- Disable continuous batching for that tenant (force immediate dispatch) to avoid head-of-line
- Route tenant to smaller model variant (eg. rwd-medium) while we triage

sam_prod: Customer-facing: we can tell AcmePay we applied a throttle and are monitoring, ask them to retry after 30s. They prefer minimal change; if we route to smaller model we need opt-in.

maria_runtime: Commands to apply throttle via control plane (ops key required):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/tenants/T-ACME-41/controls" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"max_concurrency": 2, "max_seq_length": 4096, "continuous_batching": false}'
```

raj_infra: I'm going to apply the throttle now and also temporarily bump the per-host queue depth by +32 as a stopgap (watching memory).

(90s later)

raj_infra: Throttle applied and continuous batching disabled for tenant T-ACME-41. Per-host queue depth increased by 32. Observability: queue_depth dropped from ~124 -> ~38 over the last 60s, p95 latency is decreasing.

emily_support: Updating customer: "We've applied a temporary throttle and routing adjustments to reduce tail timeouts. Please retry; we expect error rate to drop within 1-2 minutes." Sending update to CS-8421.

oncall-bot: "incident: mitigation applied by raj_infra at 2025-06-23T16:11:45Z"

kevin_sre: Follow-ups / long-term proposals:
- Add tenant-aware queue isolation: separate short/long request queues or class-of-service to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Enforce default max_seq_length for hosted tenants and offer config opt-in for long-context customers.
- Improve batching policy to cap batch hold time per-request if a request hits seq-length threshold.
- Add automated tenant throttling when queue_depth > 0.8 for X seconds.

sam_prod: Customer responds: "Errors dropped immediately after your change. Throughput reduced but acceptable. We'll work with you to reduce request lengths where possible." They asked for timeline on permanent fix.

maria_runtime: Action items:
- runtime: implement per-tenant batch timeout and limit for long-seq (P1, owner: maria_runtime)
- infra: add automated emergency throttle runbook + dashboard (P2, owner: raj_infra)
- support: coordinate with AcmePay on best-effort request size reductions (owner: sam_prod)

lee_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep monitoring p99 and queue depth for 24h.

emily_support: Thanks team. I'll close the customer loop and file the post-incident notes under CS-8421 and link to this thread. :thumbsup:

kevin_sre: One more note — check KV-cache eviction rates across the cluster. If we're evicting heavily, we should consider temporarily lowering kvcache_size for long-seq flows to avoid thrashing.

emily_support: Noted. Closing here; reopen if error rate resurges.
